clue.text: Though not yet dead, Nana is 100 and very lively

definitions.text: Though not yet dead, Nana is 100 and very lively

indicators.note: lively suggests the letters jumping about, so the fodder words are rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A spry grandmother of a hundred is still going strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lively' rearranges DEAD, NANA IS, C and VERY; the whole clue is also the definition, describing a very old person who is still alive, so 'dead' serves in both readings.
explanation.definitionFit: A centenarian granny still kicking is elderly, which is what the phrase means.

clue.text: Mammoth prank after rock concert

indicators.note: after places the prank's word behind the concert's word

parts.note: a gig is a rock or pop concert
an antic is a playful prank or caper

explanation.surface: A huge practical joke played after a rock show.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth used as an adjective is a synonym for huge.

clue.text: Beginner to try out with Oxford first

indicators.note: out suggests the word try is put out of order
first means only the opening letter of Oxford is taken

explanation.surface: A novice at a university trying out, with Oxford as first choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TRY to TYR; 'first' takes O from Oxford, the abbreviation for the city or university.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyro is a synonym for a novice or learner.

clue.text: Colour of the sea?

parts.note: read as the colour belonging to the sea service, the Royal Navy's uniform shade, rather than the water's hue

explanation.walkthrough: Many solvers first wrote DEEP BLUE; the navy is the sea-going service, whose uniform gives the dark shade its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark blue shade is named after naval uniforms, the 'sea' being the navy.

clue.text: Changes accounts about head of cows and bulls

indicators.note: about means the editing word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to edit accounts is to change them

indicators.note: head of takes the opening letter of cows

explanation.surface: Someone alters the books concerning cattle livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulls' looks like cattle beside 'cows', but means papal bulls, formal decrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal bull is a formal decree issued by the Pope.

clue.text: Cool chap with the force has battle with militants' leader

parts.note: Luke Skywalker of Star Wars uses the Force
war is a battle on a grand scale

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of militants'

explanation.surface: A calm Jedi hero fights alongside a rebel chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm means unenthusiastic, a synonym of cool in its sense of indifferent.

clue.text: Milk product from a goat?

definitions.meaning: a dairy spread churned from cream
a goat butts, so one that butts is jokingly a ...

explanation.definitionFit: Churned cream gives this spread, and a creature that butts is whimsically one too.

clue.text: Critical of Lenin's goat–herd? Not exactly before time!

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged letters ahead of the time abbreviation
not exactly suggests the words are not given in their exact order

parts.note: the name with its possessive letter, all used as fodder
the word used as fodder

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's goatherd is in a bad way, just before time runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not exactly' says the fodder is not in its exact order; the hyphen in goat-herd is ignored and the possessive S of Lenin's is used as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being critically ill in hospital is described as being on the danger list.

clue.text: Milk producer gets help after many setbacks

indicators.note: after places the help word behind the turned word
setbacks suggests the word for many goes back to front

parts.note: a myriad is a great many
aid means help

explanation.surface: A dairy worker gets assistance after many misfortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setbacks' reads the word for many backwards; 'Milk producer' suggests a cow but is the farm worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid milks cows, so she produces milk for the farm.

clue.text: Reversal for vessel after you reported last in fleet

indicators.note: after puts the vessel at the end
reported means the word you is given as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like U

indicators.note: last in takes the final letter of fleet

parts.note: an urn is a vessel or vase

explanation.surface: A ship turning round after you report it trailing the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-turn is a complete reversal of direction or policy.

clue.text: A PC crashing is like a person's hypersensitivity, say

definitions.text: A PC crashing is like a person's hypersensitivity, say

parts.words: A PC crashing is like a person's hypersensitivity, say
parts.note: a comparison between a computer failing and someone's allergic reaction is an example of a likeness drawn, and the word for it sounds like 'an allergy'

explanation.walkthrough: Boatman's original clue was longer ('crashing on certain inputs'); the comparison is an example ('say') of the answer, which also sounds like 'an allergy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparing a computer crash to an allergic reaction is drawing a parallel, the meaning of the word.

clue.text: The cat's a mean fiddler, I declare!

indicators.note: I declare suggests a spoken statement, so the words for a mean fiddler are said out loud

parts.note: a fiddler in the sense of a swindler is a cheater

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that the big cat is a nasty swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent 'cheater' is said just like the big cat's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is a large spotted wild cat, the fastest land animal.

clue.text: Refer in report to some pages on the Web?

indicators.note: in report means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a website is a set of pages on the Web

explanation.surface: Asking someone to quote what they read on a website.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite a source is to refer to it as authority.

clue.text: Doomed leaders of rescue team drown in botched sea drill

indicators.note: drown in immerses the team leaders among the other letters, so they join the same jumbled pool
botched suggests the words sea drill are messed up

parts.note: the words used as anagram fodder

indicators.note: leaders of takes the first letters of rescue and team

parts.note: first letter taken
first letter taken

explanation.surface: A lifeboat crew perishes during a disastrous training exercise at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: RT is plunged into SEA DRILL and 'botched' rearranges the lot; the two letters end up apart, so this is one pool rather than a neat insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-starred means born under an unlucky star, so fated to fail.

clue.text: Milk product I leave to emerge malleable

indicators.note: to emerge means the letters come out of the run of words

explanation.surface: A dairy item left to set into something pliable.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'proDUCT I LEave'; 'Milk' is a nod to the puzzle's dairy theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Ductile and malleable both describe metals that can be shaped without breaking.

clue.text: Stormy scenes containing unknown Boatman, first to go overboard

indicators.note: first to go places the setter's letter at the front

parts.note: the setter, Boatman, refers to himself as I

indicators.note: containing means the rearranged letters hold the unknown
stormy suggests the word scenes is tossed about

parts.note: X is the mathematician's unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Wild seas swallow a mystery sailor, the first to fall overboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy' rearranges SCENES to NECESS, X goes inside it and I comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Going overboard is doing something to excess, too much.

clue.text: Ban milk product from sheep

indicators.note: a product is something made from these ingredients, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A dairy product made from ewe's milk is prohibited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product' rearranges BAN MILK.
explanation.definitionFit: A lambkin is a young lamb, the offspring that comes from a sheep.

clue.text: Wait around — that is an intimately touching thing

parts.note: to linger is to wait around
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Hanging about, someone notices a tender, affectionate gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is worn right against the skin, so lingerie touches intimately.

clue.text: Scraped point, tucked in, took apart and tied knot

indicators.note: tucked in means the point is placed inside the other letters
apart suggests the word took is broken up and reassembled

parts.note: W, west, is a compass point
to tie the knot is to wed

explanation.surface: Someone scraped a spot, tucked it in, dismantled it and got married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraped' is the bowing-and-scraping sense; 'took apart' rearranges took and 'tucked in' puts the point inside before the wedding word.
explanation.definitionFit: To bow and scrape is to kowtow, behaving obsequiously.

clue.text: No swearing? Absurd from northerners

indicators.note: absurd suggests the words are turned into nonsense and rearranged

explanation.surface: A ban on cursing is ridiculous, say people from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: People of Norway live in northern Europe, so are northerners.

clue.text: Money back due to substance in milk product

indicators.note: back means the money word is written in reverse

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: Cash is returned owing to a component of cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TENNER around.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet is the enzyme added to milk to curdle it in cheese-making.

clue.text: Cricket in India: an exotic scent

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: exotic suggests the word scent is made strange and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket match in India has a foreign aroma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket' looks like the sport, especially beside India, but is the chirping creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is a jumping, chirping insect.

clue.text: Affectedly sweet, but pointless

indicators.note: affectedly suggests putting on airs, so the word sweet is rearranged

parts.note: pointless here names S, a compass point, as the letter missing from the jumble

explanation.surface: Something overly cute and of no use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affectedly' rearranges SWEET and 'pointless' leaves out S; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee describes something sentimentally cute to the point of being cloying.

clue.text: European leading nation has such sadly incomplete people

indicators.note: leading puts the European letter in front

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, stands in for nation here

indicators.note: sadly suggests the word such is upset and jumbled

explanation.surface: A European head of state has these unhappy, diminished folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges SUCH to UCHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrated men lack what other men have, hence incomplete people.

clue.text: Plunge into nett loss from bitter lemon mixer

indicators.note: loss from means the letters of nett are lost from the larger pool
a mixer is a drink, and the word signals the letters being mixed up

explanation.surface: Net losses from sales of a bitter lemon tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking NETT from BITTER LEMON leaves B, I, R, L, E, M, O, which 'mixer' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil is to plunge or involve someone in conflict.

clue.text: Starts with breakfast: a kipper (emulating Cook)

indicators.note: starts with takes the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Morning begins with a smoked herring, prepared in the style of a famous chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a chef's name in the surface; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bake is to cook food in an oven.

clue.text: Their wings develop no lift and shear off

indicators.note: off suggests the word shear goes wrong and is rearranged

explanation.surface: Birds' wings fail to give them lift and break off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SHEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheas are large flightless South American birds, so their wings cannot lift them.

clue.text: Spooner to select milk product with legumes

indicators.note: Spooner signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: to pick is to select
cheese is made from milk

explanation.surface: A professor chooses cheese to go with beans.
explanation.walkthrough: PICK CHEESE with first sounds swapped is said like CHICK PEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chickpeas are the seeds of a leguminous plant, so legumes.
